clue.text: Curious way to row

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a range is a row or line, as of mountains

explanation.surface: A rower with an odd technique is criticised for an unusual stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious in the sense of odd or peculiar is a plain synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Very loud, but ultimately quiet

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the neighbouring word is kept

blocks.note: so means very, as in so good
F is forte, the musical marking for loud
the last letter of but

explanation.surface: A musical direction seems to contradict itself, moving from very loud to quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a score marking, but 'Very loud' is split: 'Very' and 'loud' supply separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft and quiet are interchangeable adjectives for a sound of low volume.

clue.text: Appleyard points out reason for interruption to match

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of shape and rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words taken together

explanation.surface: A cricketer named Appleyard points out why the match has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Appleyard was a Yorkshire and England cricketer, which suits the cricket-flavoured answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain stopped play is the standard announcement when bad weather halts a cricket match, so it explains a break in the game.

clue.text: Spice Girls’ foremost fan – me, at first

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so just the opening letter is used
at first tells us the pieces just named go at the start, before the earlier one

blocks.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a fitness nut
taken as written
the first letter of Girls

explanation.surface: A self-declared superfan claims to be the Spice Girls' number one admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girls' reads as the pop group, but the two words are split: the first is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is a spice, the ground seed of a tropical evergreen tree, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: Scandalous revelation from former model

blocks.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
to model is to pose for an artist or camera

explanation.surface: A former model sells a kiss-and-tell story to the tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposé is a published report that uncovers wrongdoing or shameful secrets.

clue.text: Compartment in 16 where birds fight

blocks.note: first meaning: the pilot's cabin in a bomber, the answer to 16 down
second meaning: the enclosed arena used for cockfighting

explanation.surface: An aircraft cabin is likened to an arena for fighting birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 16 down, a bomber, so the first meaning is the pilot's seat in an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a pilot's flight-deck area in a plane and the literal pit where gamecocks were set on each other.

clue.text: Singing fellows from Switzerland in more trouble

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica
the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Swiss singers find themselves in deeper difficulty than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in more trouble' reads as a phrase, but 'in' belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Choirmen are male members of a choir, so they are men who sing together.

clue.text: Dealer, one shedding tears about publisher

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps itself around the other

blocks.note: someone who weeps is a crier
OUP is Oxford University Press, a well-known publisher

explanation.surface: A card dealer weeps over something to do with a publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford University Press is the publishing house of the University of Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a casino gaming table, dealing cards and collecting stakes, so is a dealer in that setting.

clue.text: Liquorice sweets obtained from spacecraft token

indicators.note: obtained from suggests something produced by working on raw material, so the letters are refashioned

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Someone gets sweets by handing over a token in a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Pontefract is a town in Yorkshire, England, historically the centre of British liquorice growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontefract cakes are small round black confections made of liquorice, named after the Yorkshire town where they originated.

clue.text: Article and manuscript on the little people for those very folk

blocks.note: the definite article
MS is the standard abbreviation for manuscript
elves are the little people of folklore; on means placed after in a down clue

explanation.surface: A scholarly article and a manuscript about fairy folk are written for those fairies themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Themselves is the emphatic plural pronoun, used to stress that the same people are meant.

clue.text: Loud isn’t very soft

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical marking for loud
ain't is a colloquial form of the negative verb

explanation.surface: A paradoxical claim that something loud is not quiet at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a truism about volume; the first two words are pieces and only 'very soft' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint sound is barely audible, so it can be described as extremely quiet.

clue.text: Say a word such as “it” at church

blocks.note: it is an example of a pronoun
CE is the Church of England; at simply places it next

explanation.surface: Someone is told how to say a particular word in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to utter or articulate a word, the same verb sense as saying it.

clue.text: Ruthless traders like places with tourists

blocks.note: as means like, in the sense of similar to
to place something is to set it down
day trippers are tourists; with just joins them on

explanation.surface: Cutthroat dealers are compared to holiday resorts crowded with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'places' looks like a noun for resorts, but it is the verb meaning puts.
explanation.definitionFit: Asset strippers buy companies cheaply and sell off their valuable parts for profit, a practice seen as ruthless.

clue.text: Domestic flights

blocks.note: surface reading: air travel within one country
setter's reading: flights of steps inside a home

explanation.walkthrough: A flight is also a run of steps, and domestic can mean belonging to the house rather than the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoor stepped structures linking floors of a house are flights of stairs within the home.

clue.text: God’s sign of the end of winter, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said by others, so we go by what is heard rather than written

blocks.clueFragment: sign of the end of winter
blocks.note: a thaw, melting ice and snow, signals winter is ending

explanation.surface: A deity's signal that winter is over is described.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, without a sounded final R, the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse deity of thunder, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Intellectual bookworm initially gripped by Le Carré novel

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is used
being gripped means being held inside, so one piece sits within the other
novel means new, so the letters before it are made into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the first letter of bookworm
the letters of the author's name

explanation.surface: A clever bookworm is absorbed in a John le Carré spy novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a noun for le Carré's book, but it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral describes someone driven by intellect and reasoning rather than emotion, the same adjective sense.

clue.text: Houston regularly invested in island wood tar

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
money invested in something is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Houston
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A Texan city puts money into an island's timber preservative business.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is a dark oily distillate from wood or coal, used to preserve fences and timber.

clue.text: Bomber will distort route

blocks.note: to warp is to bend or distort
a lane is a route or path, as in a shipping lane

explanation.surface: A bomber plans to bend the course of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomber is a military aircraft built to drop bombs, one kind of combat aircraft.

clue.text: Non-metric standard for beard and paper

blocks.note: first meaning: the system of feet, pounds and pints
second meaning: a small pointed tuft of hair below the lower lip
third meaning: a traditional size of sheet for printing and drawing

explanation.surface: A measurement standard is said to apply to both facial hair and paper.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a triple definition: three separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the old British measuring system, a beard style popularised by Napoleon III, and a large sheet size.

clue.text: Area of land when returning from Dover-Calais

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow
returning means going back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of Dover and the start of Calais

explanation.surface: A traveller on the return ferry from Dover to Calais thinks about a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land measuring 4,840 square yards, so it names a plot's size.

clue.text: Settle differences – or is it cosmetic?

blocks.note: first meaning: a phrasal verb for reconciling after a quarrel
second meaning: products applied to the face

explanation.surface: Is a reconciliation genuine, or merely superficial?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cosmetic' looks like an adjective meaning superficial, but it is the noun for face products.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up after a row is to be reconciled, and make-up is lipstick, powder and similar facial products.

clue.text: Law suit finally disposed of – for a figure

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so just the closing letter is used
disposed of means got rid of, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a statute is a law passed by a legislature
the last letter of suit

explanation.surface: A lawsuit is finally settled in exchange for a sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the two Ts in the law word is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted representation of a person, also called a figure.

clue.text: Ethical procedure affecting cod-piece factor

indicators.note: affecting means altering, so the letters that follow are changed in order

blocks.note: the letters of both words together

explanation.surface: Rules of conduct are being influenced by the codpiece element.
explanation.walkthrough: A codpiece is a pouch worn over the groin in Tudor dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A code of practice is a set of written rules guiding professional conduct and standards.

clue.text: Where to see toned bodies? Covers of glossy magazines!

indicators.note: covers are on the outside, so only the outermost letters of each word are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of glossy
the first and last letters of magazines

explanation.surface: Fit physiques are the usual cover images on shiny magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyms are fitness halls where people work out, so trim muscular bodies are seen there.

clue.text: It may ‘elp to seal

indicators.note: may signals a possibility, so the letters that follow could be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: the letters of the dropped-aitch help plus to and seal

explanation.surface: A Cockney speaker remarks that something could help close up a package.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a British brand of clear sticky tape helps seal parcels. Dropping the H, Cockney style, makes the letters work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sellotape is the British brand name for transparent adhesive tape, used for sealing envelopes and packages.

clue.text: Wine temperature fine

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
okay means fine or all right

explanation.surface: A wine is served at a suitable temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokay is a sweet dessert vintage from the Tokaj region of Hungary.

clue.text: Plastic cups material from messy home at the heart of the Pyrenees

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: a sty is a pigsty, a very untidy home
the middle four letters of Pyrenees

explanation.surface: Plastic beakers are made from stuff found in a scruffy house in the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Styrene is the chemical that polymerises into polystyrene, from which disposable drinking vessels are made.

clue.text: Introduction of policy agreements suits everyone

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the first letter of policy
leases are rental agreements

explanation.surface: Bringing in a new policy on agreements satisfies all parties.
explanation.definitionFit: To please is to satisfy or gratify; the phrase means it satisfies all parties, with everyone as the object.
